frameworks.name: Generational Teaching Framework
frameworks.definition: A multi-generational model where each generation forges further than the last by standing on the shoulders of predecessors, each mentor helping the next generation clear obstacles faster.

frameworks.name: Mentor-Student Progression Hierarchy
frameworks.definition: A structured view of learning where students move through sequential stages (basics, intermediate, advanced) without needing to deprecate earlier teachers when surpassing them.

claims.text: A good teacher's goal is for the student to eventually surpass them; if your students and mentees don't move above you, it means you are a bad teacher, not a good one.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: The student's advancement demonstrates the teacher's effectiveness in building a foundation and removing obstacles that would have slowed the student's progress.

claims.text: Early-stage mentors teach foundational knowledge (arithmetic, multiplication basics) that is prerequisite for advanced learning (algebra, higher concepts); early inadequacy is not the teacher's fault but rather part of the necessary sequencing.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Student progression through skill levels
Sequential knowledge building
claims.mechanism: Foundation skills must precede advanced skills; without arithmetic mastery, a student cannot understand algebra. Deprecating an earlier teacher when advancing mistakes sequencing for incompetence.
bounded_by: Does not apply to foundational teachers who actively teach incorrectly
Does not apply when previous teachers deliberately withhold critical information

claims.text: Hornmozi advanced financially beyond his early mentors and initially interpreted this as proof that he was better than them, until he realized that his advancement was only possible because they provided the headstart.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Founder has achieved higher financial outcomes than early mentors
Time horizon is medium-term (several years)
claims.mechanism: Surpassing a mentor financially does not indicate superior capability or knowledge; it indicates that the mentor's foundational contribution created the ladder the student climbed.

claims.text: Mortality and legacy reframe competitive drive: because no one will remember you 10,000 years from now, the people who matter at the end of your life are not those you vanquished but those you helped.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Late-stage reflective perspective
Focus on legacy and meaning
claims.mechanism: Competitive achievers face a psychological choice: continue zero-sum competition or redirect that energy toward helping others, which generates joy and sustainable meaning beyond financial victory.

claims.text: The joy of seeing mentees achieve results (e.g., reaching $4M revenue) makes stomaching hard times easier because the effort feels purposeful beyond personal gain.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Mentor has direct contact with mentee outcomes
Mentee success is documented and visible
claims.mechanism: Aligned purpose (mentee's outcome tied to mentor's guidance) creates intrinsic motivation that sustains the mentor through cycles of failure and plateau.

claims.text: When a mentor realizes that sharing discoveries will help many people avoid years of struggle, it reframes failure as investment in future teaching (e.g., if I figure out how to break through a $30M plateau, 100 others won't spend two years on it).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Mentor has experienced repeated failure or plateau
Mentor believes discoveries are transferable to others in similar stage
claims.mechanism: Reframing personal struggle as the cost of discovering shortcuts for others multiplies the perceived ROI of failure, reducing isolation and increasing motivation to persist.

claims.text: Mentors hold back secrets and refuse to share because they wrongly believe teaching reduces their competitive advantage; this belief is false because teaching multiplies the mentor's impact without diminishing their earnings.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Mentor operates from scarcity mindset
Mentor views mentee advancement as zero-sum loss
claims.mechanism: Information and advice are non-rival goods; sharing a shortcut does not diminish the mentor's ability to use it. Mentors who refuse to teach lose the asymmetric benefit of mentee gratitude and legacy impact.
bounded_by: Does not apply when teaching requires significant time that crowds out the mentor's own work
Does not apply to proprietary competitive secrets that are business moats, not transferable wisdom

claims.text: The purpose of progress is that each generation should have it easier than the last because the previous generation cleared the path; resentment that younger people didn't suffer as much contradicts the stated mission of 'making the world a better place.'
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Multi-generational time horizon
Explicit commitment to societal improvement
claims.mechanism: Progress compounds when each generation removes obstacles for the next, accelerating the path forward. Resenting the next generation's ease contradicts the philanthropic intent, exposing it as performative rather than genuine.

claims.text: Generation advancement math: mentors clear trees and obstacles; next generation reaches the next forest three times faster by reusing the cleared path. That generation clears the next frontier; the generation after that moves six times faster to cover both distances.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Each generation's base accelerates the next by compounding effort removal; the ratio increases because leverage compounds additively.

numbers.axis: generational acceleration ratio relative to predecessor effort

anchors.value: ~6x faster to cover Gen 0 + Gen 1 distance

claims.text: Hormoizi was stuck at $30M revenue for three years; when he shares this discovery, mentees will move past this point in weeks or months because they have the right mental model and advice he lacked.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Mentee is at similar stage ($30M revenue transition point)
Mentor has diagnosed the specific constraint blocking progress
claims.mechanism: Knowledge of the constraint accelerates solution discovery by orders of magnitude, removing the trial-and-error phase that consumed the mentor's time.
bounded_by: Requires mentee to be coachable and willing to apply advice
Requires constraint to be identical across business models (may not transfer perfectly across industries)

claims.text: Warren Buffett offered to work for Paul Graham for free, framing it as Graham being underpriced because Buffett would be the one gaining far more from the relationship; Buffett later passed Graham in his career without depicting this as superiority.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Early career phase with high uncertainty
Mentee has recognized exceptional talent in mentor
claims.mechanism: Framing mentorship as asymmetric value capture (mentee gains more) removes ego friction and clarifies that mentee advancement does not diminish mentor standing.

claims.text: Gary Vee forged much of the contemporary entrepreneur media and business blueprint that Hormozi is executing; Hormozi didn't have to solve the 'how do I create this whole thing' question because the blueprint already existed.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Field has been pioneered by an immediately-preceding generation
Blueprint is documented and replicable
claims.mechanism: Early pioneers create intellectual scaffolding that dramatically reduces the time-to-execution for followers, compressing years of R&D into weeks of implementation.

claims.text: Hormozi believes he will be 10x wealthier and own 10x more real estate by age 60 than he is now; if his mentors had mentored themselves, they would have similar ambitions for the same stage.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Age horizon is 20+ years
Economic leverage remains available
claims.mechanism: Mentorship compounds wealth by accelerating knowledge; self-mentored founders cannot compound as aggressively because they lack leverage from others' discovery.

claims.text: There are 20-year-olds in Hormozi's observation who are making twice what he was making at 30, a direct result of mentorship compression; this is the intended outcome of effective teaching, not a loss.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Mentee is in a compressed-timeline opportunity (e.g., online business, software)
Mentor has documented and shared the path
claims.mechanism: Effective mentorship removes obstacles and clarifies priority; combined with modern leverage (software, content), this accelerates timeline by 2-3x.

numbers.axis: mentee earnings at age 30 relative to mentor earnings at same age

examples.text: A person Hormozi was walking with said, 'dude, I did everything you have and we're doing $4 million a year now' — this person was emotional knowing that they had replicated success through mentorship. This example illustrates how direct mentee outcome visibility creates emotional connection for the mentor and validates the teaching effort.

When a student learns arithmetic first, then multiplication, then algebra, they do not resent their arithmetic teacher for not teaching them algebra. The earlier teacher was necessary; the sequence was the point. Hormozi initially did the opposite — deprecating early mentors once he surpassed them — until recognizing the flaw in this logic.

Warren Buffett approached Paul Graham and said 'I'll work for you for free' — Buffett recognized that he would gain more value from the relationship than Graham would, making himself a bargain even at zero cost. Graham accepted this asymmetry. Later, when Buffett surpassed Graham's career outcomes, Buffett did not depict himself as superior; instead, he credited the headstart.

Hormozi was stuck at mid-$30M revenue for three years, unable to identify why he couldn't break through. He will now be able to help mentees move past this plateau in weeks because he can explain the bottleneck he discovered. This example shows how personal struggle becomes a teaching asset; the time cost compounds backward across the entire mentee cohort.

practices.text: If a video or mentorship content changed your mind about how you treated an earlier mentor or teacher, send them a text saying 'hey, respect, I appreciate you' — do not underestimate the impact this message has on the mentor.

Recognize that you will eventually pass your mentors; when you do, do not brag or claim superiority. Instead, acknowledge that you stood on their shoulders and would not have reached that height without them.
If you are a mentor, stop holding back secrets and discoveries. Share the shortcuts you discovered so that your mentees can pass you and move faster; this is the definition of impact and progress.

When mentoring the next generation, explicitly point out obstacles and pitfalls ahead so they can avoid them — 'watch out for that hole, watch out for that rock, keep going' — so they can move three times faster than you did on the same path.
Redirect competitive drive from zero-sum comparison ('I'm better than you because I out-earned my mentor') toward contribution ('My mentor helped me, now I help others so they don't suffer as much').
